findings.F1: The book's gain does not survive its fees. The position's mean next-day gain is 0.000428 per bar, all of it timing (0.000452; the market part is -0.000025). Fees average 0.000649 per bar from a mean turnover of 0.56 of the book per bar, which leaves -0.000221 per bar after costs.
findings.F2: The fade only works when the coin's own 20-day volatility is high. In each coin's top tercile of 20-day volatility, timing is +0.001570 against fees of 0.000578, net +0.000971 (t 2.91, n 10049, Sharpe 0.56). In the bottom tercile, timing is -0.000611, net -0.001353 (t -5.89, n 10043, Sharpe -1.12). In the middle tercile, net is -0.000710 (t -2.73).
findings.F3: Next-day reversal exists only in the volatile state. In the top 20-day-volatility tercile, the next day's vol-scaled return regressed on today's vol-scaled move has slope -0.070 (t -5.78). In the bottom tercile the slope is +0.049 (t 3.46) and the lag-1 correlation is +0.034, so in calm stretches a daily move continues and the fade loses.
findings.F4: Volatility measured against the coin's own past year sorts the same way. The top quintile of 20-day vol over 250-day vol has timing +0.001457 and net +0.000562, with reversal slope -0.047 (t -2.85). The bottom quintile has net -0.000848 (t -2.76), with continuation slope +0.068 (t 2.90).
findings.F5: The high-volatility tercile pays net in every year except 2024. Net returns were +0.0030 in 2018, +0.0017 in 2019, +0.0025 in 2020, +0.0008 in 2021, +0.0008 in 2022, +0.0013 in 2023, -0.0009 in 2024 and +0.0002 in 2025. The low-volatility tercile lost net in six of eight years, worst in 2024 (-0.0035) with n 2102. So the failure of the book's later years, and of its leave-one-window-out Sharpe, comes from calm-state bars.
findings.F6: Bigger fades earn more but still barely clear their fees. In the top fifth by |forecast|, timing is 0.001583 against fees of 0.000980. The second fifth loses (timing -0.000118, fee 0.000485). The book's small positions are mostly fee-paying noise.

ideas.idea: A coin's daily move is followed by a move the other way over the next day, and the larger the move and the higher the coin's 20-day volatility, the larger the move back, only while the coin's 20-day volatility is high relative to its own volatility over the past year.
ideas.consequence: A trader would fade daily moves only in a coin's volatile stretches, sizing with the move and the volatility, and would stay out of the fade in calm and ordinary stretches where it loses more than its fees.
ideas.name: Fade only in volatile stretches

ideas.idea: In a coin whose 20-day volatility is low relative to its own past year, a daily move is followed by a move the same way over the next day, and the larger the move measured in units of the 20-day volatility, the larger the continuation.
ideas.consequence: A trader would follow, not fade, a coin's daily move during its calm stretches, sizing with the move's size in volatility units.
ideas.name: Calm-stretch daily moves continue
